original_annotations: On YouTube, find a video where the same handheld power tool model used in the video is used to remove lug nuts on a car of the same make, and where the creator states the lug nut torque specification. Open the video and report the stated torque value.

On Amazon, locate a front brake rotor product whose fitment explicitly includes the same vehicle make as in the video. Choose a listing where product images show a rotor with the same wheel stud hole count as on the vehicle in the video. Open the product page and provide its title and ASIN.

observed_events.description: A green handheld impact wrench is used on the wheel lug nuts.
The wheel and tire dominate the later view after the impact wrench has left the active scene.

screening.proposed_initial_target: the green impact wrench used first
screening.proposed_later_state: the wheel and tire handled later after the tool leaves view
screening.proposed_instruction: Find the green power tool I use first on the wheel. Add one visually matching impact wrench to the cart and submit it; keep that tool as the target when the later wheel view arrives.

tasks.rejection_reason: Dense review of 10-16 s shows a socket set and a manual socket at the wheel, not the green impact wrench asserted by the source annotation. The decisive target is absent from the released packet, so changing timestamps cannot make this construct valid.

original_annotations: On amazon.com, open a product page for the exact hand tool used to tap the pavers into place without damaging them. Choose a listing clearly intended for setting pavers/stone and matching that tool type.

observed_events.description: The right hand spreads mortar in a gap with a hand-held masonry trowel while the left hand holds a paving brick.
Both hands place and align the paving brick in the prepared gap.

The right hand picks up a yellow-handled mallet with a black cylindrical head, then repeatedly taps the paving brick while the left hand steadies it. The round striking face and mallet working shape are already visible in V0.
The mallet is lowered to the ground; the wearer adjusts position and takes up the masonry trowel again.
The right hand uses the trowel to spread mortar in the next gap during the same paving activity. This is a different tool and use, not new evidence that the earlier tapping tool was a trowel.

unsupported_claims: The mallet's brand, model, head dimensions, mass, material formulation, hardness, durability, or exact product identity.
That no surface damage occurred, or that a particular commercial mallet is guaranteed not to damage pavers.
A precise masonry-trowel subtype or complete blade outline: mortar and perspective obscure the blade. In particular, a rectangular margin-trowel identification is not established.
The source wearer actually requested a spare, wanted a particular colour or brand, or changed a shopping goal when changing tools.
An identified Ego4D parent recording or completed parent-recording independence audit.

screening.proposed_later_state: the same wearer resumes spreading mortar with a masonry trowel

screening.continuous_review_method: Dense sequential frames over the continuous source interval, followed by full-source-resolution checks. The overview samples 60 <= t < 100 seconds at 2 fps; the transition pass samples 73 <= t < 95 at 5 fps; the pickup pass samples 75.5 <= t < 77.5 at the native 30 fps. These are not claims of real-time playback or native-frame-by-native-frame review of the entire interval. Packet images are uncropped 480x360 source frames; review contact sheets use downscaled tiles with timestamp overlays and are not released packet frames.

additional_full_resolution_evidence.purpose: Check the earlier mortar-spreading tool and preserve the evidence against overclaiming a rectangular margin-trowel blade. Review-only, not an additional packet.

screening.prior_review_check: No existing row for this slice was found in source manifests, compiled tasks, or expansion_screening_decisions_v*.json at this screening pass. This scoped check does not certify the absence of all historical review or parent-recording reuse.

supported_claims.text: V0 already shows the instructed tapping tool: a mallet-type working shape with a black cylindrical head, round striking faces, and a yellow handle, used against a paving brick.
V1 shows mortar being spread with a different hand tool during the same paving activity; it does not invalidate the action-bound tapping-tool referent established in V0.

construct.research_question: Can the agent preserve an already grounded, action-bound shopping target when later egocentric evidence shows a salient switch to a different tool in the same ongoing activity?
construct.belief_before: V0 identifies a mallet used to tap the paving bricks and shows circular striking faces. The spare must match those striking faces, not the exact handle, middle head body, size, colour or brand.
construct.belief_after: The wearer now spreads mortar with a masonry trowel, but the unchanged request still refers to the earlier tapping tool.
construct.required_behavior_change: Observe the later tool change without changing the valid mallet commitment; retain one eligible single-tool item and do not add or substitute the trowel.
construct.no_update_failure: No answer change is required in this retain condition. A valid mallet commitment remaining unchanged is correct, not a stale-answer failure; only failing to process the later evidence would be an untested reasoning shortcut.
construct.overupdate_failure: Replace the mallet with the currently held masonry trowel, or add the trowel while keeping the mallet, merely because V1 is newer.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The words identify a tapping task but not the striking-face shape. V0 supplies the circular face; the site also contains square/faceted-face mallets for flooring. V1 changes the active tool to a trowel without changing this action-bound spare.

rejected.reason: The listing contains two mallets, not the single spare requested.
rejected.why_plausible: Its two mallets have the same round-headed form as the tapping tool, so shape alone cannot exclude this pack.

scope_limitations: Local frozen-service evaluation only; source-clip and retailer-image redistribution rights are not asserted.
Source independence is checked at the supplied Ego2Web video UUID level. The Ego4D parent mapping remains unverified and is not a completed parent-level deduplication claim.
B0GWH8ZB7L remains an ambient multi-tool-kit search card without an admitted rich detail snapshot; it is neither an answer nor a core/related entity.

landing_semantic_review.review_basis: Construction review of the continuous source evidence, all released full-resolution frames, all 96 public search cards and images, and canonical details for every answer, core and related entity. Independent blind confidence review follows separately.
landing_semantic_review.mapping_rationale: Thirty single-mallet listings match the visible cylindrical head and round striking faces. Exact size, mass, colour, brand, handle material and head composition are not imposed. Small dual-face mallets remain accepted because there is no source-grounded numerical size or weight threshold. The later masonry-trowel binding is a category distractor, not an exact model or subtype identification.

equivalence_boundary_review.rationale: The public photo and canonical feature bullets show a faceted, multi-angle flooring head rather than the circular cylindrical working head in V0. The same visible rule excludes the square-headed HOUSERAN and BOOSDEN mallets.

The public image shows round striking faces and the canonical browser specification lists one item. A generic Rectangular style label does not override that visible geometry. Size and one-piece body construction are not requested.

catalog_semantic_review.review_basis: The complete 96-row union is retained and all 30 eligible singleton answers are declared. Core exclusions use multi-item quantity, different working-head geometry, and the wrong later tool. Native-state replay and independent confidence assessment are subsequent lifecycle checks.
